gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-asap: Smooth curves, tall lowercase, daylight between the letters: that's Wallpoet. Wallpoet is best at announcing a line with loud, high-standing shapes, while Asap, a sans-serif body, does its best work staying readable, its c forms open arcs.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-supreme: Junegull has a retro, friendly look, with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye. Supreme lays down a dense, heavy-looking strip of text, crisp and open enough to carry paragraph after paragraph.
gen-eater-switzer: Switzer reads friendly and Swiss, its wire-like strokes tracing each letter at constant weight. And Eater brings dark, aggressive menace on top, with widely spaced letters and a gentle thick-thin rhythm.
gen-irish-grover-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads clean and professional, with a larger-than-usual x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends. Irish Grover is the fun, sturdy shouter; Fira Sans is the tidy worker.
gen-dafont-visitor-satoshi: Nostalgic digital charm: Visitor's solder-pulled strokes meet Satoshi's tall lowercase and wide-open e, which never looks squeezed shut. What stands out is Visitor's gaping mouths set against Satoshi's approachable ease.
gen-flavors-manrope: Whimsical and a bit commanding, Flavors towers in its lowercase, diagonals carrying the same heft as its stems. Manrope, a sans-serif with bright open curves, can sit at a modest size beneath it.
gen-gf-goldman-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads trustworthy, with a hefty lowercase body and broad open counters on c and s. But Goldman pushes wide, bold letters with round forms like open parentheses, a decidedly louder partner.
gen-gf-gugi-montserrat: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, with terminals cut open so counters flow outward. Gugi is best at bold, distinctive punch, while Montserrat is best at gliding, approachable geometry.
gen-luckiest-guy-archivo: Luckiest Guy is cheerful and loud, its letters like bent tubing. Archivo, a sans-serif with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, then gives long paragraphs an editorial, approachable footing.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-satoshi: Satoshi reads approachable, with a wide-open e that never looks squeezed. Neuropolitical is best at pulled-apart, geometric, neon-tube display lines, while Satoshi is best at tall, uniform-stroke text.
